questions.question: 34 is related to 191 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 56 is related to 301. To which of the following is 63 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
34 is related to 191 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 56 is related to 301. To which of the following is 63 related, following the same logic?
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution: Logic: (1st number × 5) + 21 = 2nd number. Similarly, for 63 ∶ ? ⇒ (63 × 5) + 21 = 315 + 21 = 336.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 5 related to 2 if ‘5 ÷ 1 × 3 ÷ 4 − 2’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, how is 5 related to 2 if ‘5 ÷ 1 × 3 ÷ 4 − 2’?
questions.solution:
5 is the father of 1, 1 is the wife of 3, 3 is the father of 4 and 4 is the brother of 2.

​

So, 5 is the "Mother's father" of 2.

questions.question: What will come in place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged? 63 × 9 + 21 – 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

63 × 9 + 21 – 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 63 × 9 + 21 – 4 ÷ 5 = ?

After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 63 ÷ 9 - 21 + 4 × 5 = ? ⇒ ? = 7 - 21 + 4 × 5 ⇒ ? = 7 - 21 + 20 ⇒ ? = 27 - 21 = 6

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All computers are printers. Some printers are laptops. All laptops are mobiles. Conclusions: I. Some printers are computers. II. Some laptops are printers. III. Some mobiles are laptops.

Statements:

Some printers are laptops.
All laptops are mobiles.
Conclusions:
I. Some printers are computers.
II. Some laptops are printers.
III. Some mobiles are laptops.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some printers are computers. - True (because All computers are printers so, Some printers are computers too)

II. Some laptops are printers. - True (because Some printers are laptops so, Some laptops are printers too)

III. Some mobiles are laptops. - True (because All laptops are mobiles so, Some mobiles are laptops too)

questions.question: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged
31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

Given equation: 31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 31 × 3 + 186 ÷ 6 – 17 = ?

⇒ 31 × 3 + 186 ÷ 6 – 17 = ?

⇒ 93 + 186 ÷ 6 – 17 = ?

⇒ 93 + 31 – 17 = ?

⇒ 124 – 17 = ?

⇒ 107.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
